aliases: hamming code: locating one flipped bit
purpose: How can three overlapping checks tell us which bit changed?
meaning: A (7,4) Hamming code block adds three parity bits to four data bits. With even parity, the checks on positions 1,3,5,7; 2,3,6,7; and 4,5,6,7 produce bits s₁, s₂ and s₄. Their weighted sum s=s₁+2s₂+4s₄ is the syndrome. With no flip it is zero; with one flipped bit it gives that bit’s ordinary position from one through seven. This single-error correction step restores the encoded block and the original four-bit data.

definition.setting: A workshop sends a four-bit machine-status label d through a wire as a seven-bit block c. Three added check bits overlap the data positions. Choose either a single flipped bit position j or no flip, then follow the received block r through its three parity checks into the repaired label u.

conditions: Use a whole data value d from 0 to 15 and a whole flip selection j from 0 to 7. Zero selects no flip; actual bit positions are numbered one through seven. The guarantee assumes at most one flipped bit in the entire seven-bit block. Data bits occupy positions 3,5,6,7 and even-parity bits occupy positions 1,2,4.
definition.domain_notes: This deterministic construction does not simulate random noise or an extended SECDED code. Multiple errors can make the single-error decoder repair the wrong position. Zero syndrome does not prove error-free transmission outside the at-most-one-error assumption. The three checks and the recovered four-bit label are distinct quantities.

properties.claim: A (7,4) Hamming code block adds three parity bits to four data bits. With even parity, the checks on positions 1,3,5,7; 2,3,6,7; and 4,5,6,7 produce bits s₁, s₂ and s₄. properties.derivation: Choose parity bits so the three selected-position sums are zero modulo two. If position j changes, each check changes exactly when the corresponding binary digit of j is one. The three check results therefore spell the binary representation of j, and s₁+2s₂+4s₄=j. A second change at that same position restores all seven bits. With no flip all checks remain zero and no repair is performed.

steps.reason: Choose the four-bit data label and no flip or an ordinary flipped position.

Choose parity bits so the three selected-position sums are zero modulo two. If position j changes, each check changes exactly when the corresponding binary digit of j is one. The data label is 0101. Checks one and two fail, so the syndrome is three. Repairing position three restores the original label.
